key_insight: Co-PiLOT turns inverse design into a constrained search in a learned latent space, using a generative decoder as a validity prior and a physics-informed optimizer to find target microstructures more efficiently.
engineering_relevance: This gives materials engineers a practical framework for designing magnesium alloy microstructures/texture with fewer expensive crystal-plasticity simulations while preserving feasibility.
method: Train a ViT-based encoder with latent diffusion, diffusion transformer, or rectified-flow transformer decoders to learn a compact microstructure latent space.
Use the decoder plus a self-segmenting orientation codec to map latent candidates into valid solver-ready EBSD-style inputs.
Optimize the latent codes with MERIDIAN: deep-kernel GP uncertainty, failure-aware feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On an ~80,000-image EBSD-derived dataset, the ViT-FMDiT model with z=768 achieved FID 27.86 and MS-SSIM 0.178, and with 160 simulations outperformed seven baselines by reducing relative target error by 3–22%.
watch_item: The approach depends on a high-quality learned decoder and may be sensitive to distribution shift or reconstruction fidelity when transferring to new materials systems or processing conditions.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
